key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:040E
name: start_disk_read_when_flagged
description: Checks a shared status flag and, only when it is set, waits a short fixed delay, programs the disk DMA pointer and disk length registers, calls two routines and then clears the flag. When the flag is clear it returns a failure value without touching the hardware.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:0476
name: start_disk_transfer_if_flagged
description: Checks the same shared status flag and, when set, calls routines and programs the disk DMA pointer and control registers before clearing the flag. It returns a failure value when the flag is clear, so it is the variant without the delay loop.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:04DC
name: wait_for_interrupt_request_bit
description: Polls the interrupt request register until one particular bit is set, then clears that request by writing the register again and returns the bit's value. It is a busy-wait on a single hardware event.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:04F4
name: step_disk_head_to_track
description: Compares a requested track number, which must be below 160, with the last track stored, then pulses the drive step and direction control bits once per track of difference, with a delay for each step. Out-of-range requests are ignored.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:056A
name: step_head_to_next_track
description: Increments the stored current track number, stopping at the last track, and sends one head step pulse through the drive control bits with a delay. Even and odd track counts set the control bits differently.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:05BE
name: recalibrate_disk_head
description: Sets a drive control bit, waits with delays while a drive status line stays active, then resets the stored track position to zero and clears a related control bit. It returns the head to a known starting track.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:060A
name: set_drive_select_bit
description: Sets the high bit of a shadow control byte together with the bit indexed by the byte's own low three bits, which selects one drive line. The routine only updates the shadow value and does not call anything.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:063A
name: clear_drive_select_bit
description: Clears the high bit and the bit indexed by the shadow control byte's low three bits, which deselects the drive line, then calls one routine. It is the inverse of the matching select routine.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:065A
name: wait_for_disk_status_clear
description: Waits a fixed delay, then busy-waits while a disk status bit in the shadow control byte remains set. It returns once that status bit is clear.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:0672
name: wait_for_status_bit_edge
description: Waits while a status bit is set and then waits until it is set again, so it returns on the next rising edge of that status line. It is used to synchronise with a drive signal.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:068A
name: decode_mfm_words_to_bytes
description: Loops over a count of source words, shifting each word through a 32-bit register to pick out its data bits and writes one assembled byte per source word to the destination buffer. The pattern matches decoding MFM-encoded disk data.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:06A2
name: extract_odd_bits_byte
description: Shifts a 32-bit value eight times, gathering the spread-out data bits into one byte, and returns that value with one byte position masked out. It is a bit-compaction step used by the decoder.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:06B4
name: encode_bytes_to_mfm_words
description: Takes each source byte, shifts its eight bits out one at a time and inserts clock bits between data bits where neighbours are zero, writing one encoded word per byte to the destination. This is MFM encoding of data for writing to disk.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:06DA
name: encode_word_to_mfm
description: Encodes the two bytes of a 16-bit word into MFM clock and data bits using the same shift-and-insert-clock steps, leaving the 32-bit result in a register. It feeds the byte-to-MFM encoder.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:0758
name: fill_buffer_alternating_pattern
description: Fills a block of 4000 long words in memory, starting at a fixed buffer address, with an alternating bit pattern. It prepares a buffer with a known fill before disk data is written into it.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:0770
name: clear_block_and_stamp_entries
description: Clears a block of 1750 long words, then writes a marker byte and an offset value derived from the argument into three entries at fixed spacing. It initialises a track table and places marker entries in it.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:07A4
name: write_mfm_sync_marks
description: Calls one routine and then stores the standard Amiga disk sync word at six fixed memory locations spaced through the track buffer. It writes the sync marks that let the disk reader find sector boundaries.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:07E4
name: apply_track_and_run_sequence
description: Copies the stored track number into the shadow control byte, then calls four routines in sequence. It is a fixed step sequence used when moving to a track.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:0802
name: delay_until_counter_wraps
description: Counts a 16-bit register down in a tight loop until it wraps past zero, creating a fixed delay with no other effect. Other routines use it to pause between hardware operations.

key: 3D Galax/3D Galax.adf:3DGalax.boot (raw code file, load address unknown):0:0818
name: copy_track_chunks_to_output
description: Copies a 16-byte record from a table into working variables, then copies the track buffer to an output pointer in chunks, calling routines between chunks until the remaining count reaches zero. It moves decoded track data to its destination.

name: dispatch_through_stored_pointers
description: Stores an address into a fixed slot, calls one routine, then calls a routine through a function pointer kept in a table and another through a pointer held in memory. It is a small trampoline that passes control to code held in memory.

name: initialise_drive_and_load_disk
description: Turns off DMA and interrupts, clears a large memory block, copies a block of code into place and runs a bounded retry loop over drive control routines while the drive is busy. The decompiler listing is cut off, so later steps are not described.

name: call_table_routine_keep_result
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer stored at a fixed offset in a table and returns the value that was in the data register on entry. It forwards a result unchanged.

name: lookup_named_table_entry
description: Searches a table of 16-byte entries by comparing character strings, then steps through a list of codes and calls a routine for each one until a count runs out. Selector value 5 stores the table pointer and checks a four-character tag against known strings to choose a mode.

name: call_handler_keep_registers
description: Calls a handler through a function pointer stored at a fixed offset and returns the two input register values concatenated as a 64-bit result. It passes the caller's inputs through unchanged.

name: call_three_routines_in_order
description: Calls three routines one after another and returns, with a conditional return that makes no difference to the result. It is a plain sequence of calls.

name: unpack_packed_data_backwards
description: Unpacks a compressed stream by reading bits from a buffer, either copying a run of already written bytes or writing literal bytes, and it fills the destination from its end towards its start. It is a depacker for packed data.

name: shift_bit_buffer_by_count
description: Shifts a 32-bit bit buffer right by a count of bits, pulling in the previous longword from memory whenever the buffer empties and setting its top bit. It is the bit-input step used by the depacker.

name: stub_corrupt_data_exit
description: A bare return with no work, referenced next to the text 'Sorry, data are corrupted!'. It appears to be an error exit for corrupt data, but in this code it does nothing.

name: disable_hardware_and_start_loader
description: Disables all DMA channels, interrupts and disk-controller flags, zeroes a large block of memory from the start of low memory upwards, then waits on a routine until its result is non-negative before starting the main loader sequence. The listing is cut off, so the later steps are not described.

name: read_disk_block_with_retries
description: Dispatches on a request code, and for the read case it selects the drive, waits on the drive status line with a bounded countdown and retries up to six times before reporting failure. It sets the disk control register with the set bit when finished.

name: poll_disk_status_word
description: Sets a status bit, clears a result field and then calls routines to poll a status word, stopping as soon as that word becomes non-zero. It is the status poll used by the disk read routine.

name: seek_disk_track_with_retries
description: Records a non-negative track request and positions the head with two routine calls, or otherwise selects the drive and tries up to three times to move the head, waiting on a status line with a bounded countdown. It returns an error value after the last failed attempt.

name: search_name_table_for_match
description: Compares a 12-character name with up to 192 sixteen-byte table entries, stopping at the first match or at the end of the table. It returns nothing, leaving the match position to the caller.

name: read_sector_blocks_from_track
description: Looks up the record for a track, scans a 12-slot sector map for the requested sector, updates the sector and half-track flags when they change and then reads blocks of 1024 bytes until the requested amount is used up. It is the track-to-block reader for the disk loader.

name: verify_read_length_match
description: Calls two routines and, when the requested length is exactly 1024 bytes, compares two returned values and sets a -4 error status if they differ. It checks that a block read returned the expected data length.

name: pause_for_short_delay
description: Counts a 16-bit register down through 512 iterations to create a short fixed delay. Other routines use it between hardware accesses.

name: wait_status_bit_then_mark
description: Busy-waits until bit 1 of a 16-bit status field in a device record is set, then writes the value 2 into another field of the same record. It is a handshake step on a device structure.

name: call_then_await_status_clear
description: Calls one routine and then busy-waits while a disk status bit in the shadow control byte is set. It returns when that status bit clears.

name: wait_until_status_bit_set
description: Busy-waits until bit 4 of the shadow control byte becomes set, which is the drive status line going active. It returns once the line is set.

name: write_gap_and_sync_header
description: Writes a block of alternating gap words and the disk sync word into a buffer, sets the disk controller for write mode, then tries up to six times to read back a header longword that matches an expected pattern, recording an error when none matches.

name: step_head_towards_target
description: Repeatedly moves the stored track register one step at a time towards the requested track, sending a direction and a step pulse through the drive control bits for each step.

name: call_two_return_first
description: Calls one routine, then calls a second routine, and returns the value produced by the first one.

name: call_routine_pass_value
description: Calls one routine and returns the value that was in the data register when the routine was entered. It forwards an input unchanged.

name: repeat_step_pulses_until_clear
description: Repeats a sequence of drive control pulses while a status bit stays set, then clears a stored counter field. It finishes a head movement.

name: deselect_drive_unit
description: Clears the high control bit, reads a drive unit number from the caller's record, clears that unit's select bit and calls two routines. It releases a drive after an operation.

name: pulse_drive_select_line
description: Sets the high control bit and the selected unit's select bit, calls a routine, clears the select bit, calls another routine and sets it again. It strobes the drive select line.

name: merge_odd_even_bit_words
description: Combines pairs of source words by taking the data bits from each pair using an alternate-bit mask and writes one merged word per pair to the destination. It recombines the separated odd and even bits of encoded disk data.

name: call_routine_keep_input
description: Calls one routine and returns the data register value it received on entry. It is a pass-through wrapper.

name: call_routine_forward_value
description: Calls one routine and returns the value that was in the data register on entry. It forwards its input unchanged.

name: wait_for_raster_lines
description: Waits until the high byte of the video beam's vertical position changes the given number of times, which counts that many scanlines of raster time. It is a timing delay tied to the display.

name: reset_hardware_and_restart_loader
description: Sets up the hardware, clears a block of memory and runs a disk-loading sequence with timed waits and retry loops, disabling DMA and interrupts and jumping back to the start when it fails. The listing is cut off, so later steps are unknown.

name: update_moving_object_positions
description: Walks a table of up to eight moving entries and, for each active one, adds its velocity to its position and advances its data pointer, calling a routine per entry. An entry whose data marks it as finished is deactivated.

name: advance_entry_along_path
description: Reads the next offset from a path table, adds it to the entry's position when it is valid, advances the table pointer and calls a routine. It moves one entry a single step along its path.

name: spawn_fixed_entry_periodically
description: Advances a frame counter and, when it reaches fifteen with no pending path data, claims the first free slot in an eight-entry table and fills it with fixed starting values. It creates a new entry at a set interval.

name: spawn_seeded_entry_periodically
description: Advances a frame counter and, when it reaches twenty-three, claims the first free slot in an eight-entry table and fills it with a starting position derived from a seed value. It creates entries at a set interval.

name: spawn_toggling_entry_periodically
description: Advances a counter and, at a fixed count with an unset flag, toggles a state byte and claims a free table slot, choosing between two data pointers and starting positions by that state. It alternates between two kinds of entry.

name: arm_entry_once_when_clear
description: If a flag byte is zero, sets it and writes a data pointer and three values into the first table slot. It arms a single entry the first time it runs.

name: start_loader_stage_and_restart
description: Sets up display fields and calls routines, then either runs a finish sequence through jump vectors and returns, or restarts the hardware setup from the top when a flag is clear. The listing is cut off, so the later steps are not described.

name: finish_with_optional_vector_call
description: When the low flag bit is set, calls a routine through a jump vector, then writes a fixed value into the shadow flag byte. It is the closing step of a loader stage.

name: swap_bitplane_buffer_pointers
description: Toggles a state byte between two frame buffer addresses and writes five buffer pointers into the display list, each stored as a high and a low word and spaced 8800 bytes apart. It flips between two display buffers.

name: set_bitplane_pointers_five
description: Writes five buffer pointers, stored as high and low words and spaced 8800 bytes apart, into the display list from a fixed start address. It sets up the display's bitplane addresses.

name: set_bitplane_pointers_four
description: Writes four buffer pointers, stored as high and low words and spaced 16000 bytes apart, into the display list from a fixed start address. It points the display's bitplanes at the frame memory.

name: start_block_command_and_wait
description: Stores a restart address and a saved value into a control block, clears several control fields, sets the command fields and then waits while a busy bit in the status byte remains set. It starts a block operation and waits for it to finish.

name: flash_background_while_waiting
description: Calls a routine repeatedly while it returns a non-zero value, setting the background colour register to a bright blue shade and then to black around each call. It gives visual feedback during a wait.

name: wait_until_beam_past_line
description: Calls a routine repeatedly while it returns a non-zero value, and stops early once the video beam's vertical position passes a fixed scanline. It is a bounded wait tied to the display.

name: busy_wait_on_beam_position
description: Busy-waits on the video beam's vertical position word until a fixed comparison of its high byte is met. It is a timing wait tied to the display scanlines.

name: unpack_iff_body_packbits
description: Searches memory for the chunk identifier BODY, the picture data chunk of an IFF file, then decompresses the data that follows with run-length packing: a negative count repeats the next byte and other counts copy literal bytes. The output is written to a series of destination pointers.

name: unpack_iff_body_packbits_alt
description: Decompresses the BODY chunk of an IFF file with the same run-length packing as its sibling routine, but writes to a different set of destination pointers. It handles a second buffer layout.

name: unpack_iff_body_packbits_variant
description: Decompresses the BODY chunk of an IFF file using run-length packing, with a different set of destination pointers and a four-entry table. It is a third buffer layout of the same unpacker.

name: describe_unresolved_routine
description: No pseudo-code could be produced for this routine, so its purpose is not known. The facts show six instructions, three unnamed callers and no hardware register or text references.

name: unpack_packed_data_checked
description: Unpacks a compressed stream by reading bits from a buffer, copying earlier runs or writing literal bytes backwards from the end of the destination. It returns the final bit buffer value when a checksum matches and an error value otherwise.

name: unpack_packed_bits_entry
description: A shorter entry into the bit-driven depacker loop that reads bits, writes literal bytes, copies earlier runs backwards and returns a status. It returns an error value when the checksum does not match.

name: unpack_packed_bits_mid_entry
description: Another entry point into the depacker loop, reached part way through the bit-reading steps. It shares the run-copy and literal-copy logic with the other depacker routines.

name: unpack_packed_bits_tail_entry
description: A third entry point into the depacker loop that starts with a run copy and then handles literal bytes. It shares the depacker logic and returns a status at the end.

name: return_failure_status
description: Returns the failure value without doing any other work. It reports failure.

name: advance_bit_buffer_by_count
description: Shifts a 32-bit bit buffer right by a count of bits, pulling in the previous longword from memory when the buffer empties and setting its top bit. It is the bit-input step of the depacker.

name: fill_block_rows_with_word
description: Runs sixteen passes and on each pass writes a word value repeatedly across a count of words into a destination buffer, calling routines to produce each value. It fills a block with rows of data.

name: fade_colour_toward_target
description: Moves a 12-bit colour value one step at a time toward a target, adjusting each four-bit component separately. It returns early when the top component would overshoot.

name: count_interrupt_event
description: Sets a flag byte to a fixed value, writes a bit to a status register to acknowledge one interrupt source and increments a counter. It is an interrupt handler body that counts events.

name: wait_for_flag_set
description: Clears a flag byte in a control block and busy-waits until another part of the program sets it to a non-zero value. It blocks until the flag is raised elsewhere.

name: wait_for_counter_then_reset
description: Calls a routine repeatedly until a counter field in the control block reaches two, then resets that counter to zero. It waits for two events before continuing.

name: store_bitmap_dimensions
description: Stores a width and a height, computes the number of bytes per row as width divided by eight, and the total size as bytes per row times height, then clears a related counter. It records the size of a bitmap for later drawing code.

name: store_pair_of_values
description: Stores its two register arguments into two global variables. It records a pair of values for later use.

name: blit_rows_into_bitplane
description: Sets up the blitter registers for copying rows of pixel data into a bitplane, choosing a control word variant from the flags and looping over rows and planes, with each row waiting for the blitter before it starts. The listing is cut off, so not every case is described.

name: clip_horizontal_span
description: Checks a horizontal span against clip limits: when one flag is set it counts how many sixteen-pixel columns to skip at the left edge, and when another flag is set it checks the right edge. It returns the adjusted values or an error code when the span is outside the clip area.

name: enable_four_dma_channels
description: Calls four routines, enables the four lowest DMA channels in the DMA control register and writes four fixed control bytes to the shadow register. It starts DMA after setup.

name: record_slot_size_and_pointers
description: Looks up a slot index in a small table, calls a routine, stores two halved size values from the returned record into the slot and then stores a pointer and a pointer offset by a second argument. It records an entry's size and location.

name: walk_null_terminated_list
description: Walks a zero-terminated list of long words, calling a routine for each entry until a zero entry is reached. It runs an action over every entry of the list.

name: copy_slot_header_bytes
description: Looks up a slot, copies three source bytes into a per-slot buffer and sets four pointers in that slot to an address nine bytes before the source. It keeps a copy of a header for later use.

name: walk_list_until_null
description: Walks a zero-terminated list of long words, calling a routine for each entry until a zero entry is found. It is the same list walk as its sibling routines.

name: call_two_routines_then_return
description: Calls two routines in turn and returns. It is a plain two-step sequence.

name: update_slot_control_bytes
description: Looks up a slot, calls four routines and, when a control byte stored in the slot is not the sentinel value, copies two bytes into the shadow control registers. It refreshes the control state for a slot.

name: call_routines_when_flag_clear
description: Calls three routines and then calls four more only when a word flag is zero. It runs an optional group of steps.

name: disable_low_dma_channels
description: Sets the shadow control byte to one and clears the lowest four DMA channel enable bits, which turns those DMA channels off.

name: clear_control_block_region
description: Zeroes a region of bytes inside a control block, starting at a fixed offset and running up to a second fixed offset. It resets the block's working fields.

name: run_three_routine_steps
description: Calls three routines in order and returns. It is a plain three-step sequence.

name: update_slot_size_and_pointers
description: Looks up a slot, calls one routine and stores halved width and height values from a record into the slot together with a pointer and a second pointer offset by a size value. It updates the slot's size and location.

name: search_for_four_byte_tag
description: Scans memory from the current pointer up to an end pointer, comparing four bytes at each position with the value in the data register, and returns when a match is found or the end is reached. It searches for a four-character tag.

name: walk_null_list_calling_routine
description: Walks a zero-terminated list of long words, calling a routine for each entry until a zero entry is reached. It is another copy of the list walk.

name: copy_slot_header_bytes
description: Looks up a slot, copies three source bytes into a per-slot buffer and sets four pointers in that slot to an address nine bytes before the source. It keeps a copy of a header for later use.

name: walk_null_terminated_list
description: Walks a zero-terminated list of long words, calling a routine for each entry until a zero entry is reached. It runs an action over every entry of the list.

name: return_stack_argument
description: Returns the value in the first stack argument slot without changing anything else. It passes a stack argument straight back to the caller.

name: call_two_routines_in_order
description: Calls two routines in order and returns. It is a plain two-step sequence.

name: call_four_routines_keep_input
description: Calls four routines in order and returns the data register value it received on entry. It forwards its input after the calls.

name: reset_slot_fields_from_seed
description: Copies a stored value from offset eight into the first long word of a record, sets a status byte to minus one and clears two further bytes of the record. It initialises the record's state.

name: update_slot_timer_controls
description: Looks up a slot, calls four routines and, when a control byte stored in the slot is not the sentinel value, copies two bytes into the shadow control registers. The routines it calls touch the CIA timer registers.

name: rotate_byte_and_reset_state
description: When bit zero of the argument is set, stores a pointer into a record, clears a word and clears a status byte. It always returns the argument rotated right by one bit.

name: call_five_routines_return
description: Calls five routines in order and returns the value that was in the data register on entry. It is a plain five-step sequence.

name: store_record_bytes_when_flagged
description: When bit zero of the flag argument is set, stores two bytes of the value into a record, also stores a third byte when a status byte is clear, and clears one more byte. It records a value only when the flag asks for it.

name: disable_selected_dma_channels
description: Mirrors four flag bits into a shadow byte and writes each selected channel to the DMA control register with the set bit clear, which turns those DMA channels off. It shuts down chosen audio DMA channels.

name: call_four_routines_then_return
description: Calls four routines in sequence and returns. It is a plain four-step sequence.

name: arm_record_state_when_flagged
description: When bit zero of the flag argument is set, writes four bytes into a record: a one, the argument byte twice and a sentinel value of 255. It arms the record's state only when the flag is set.

name: call_routines_when_flag_clear
description: Calls three routines and then calls four more only when a word flag is zero. It runs an optional group of steps.

name: cycle_countdown_field_to_five
description: Sets a countdown field to five when it is zero, otherwise decrements it. The countdown restarts at five after reaching zero.

name: run_four_routine_steps
description: Calls four routines in order and returns. It is a plain four-step sequence.

name: copy_three_bytes_from_source
description: When a counter byte in the referenced record is zero, copies three bytes from the source data at the given index into three fields of the current record. It loads a three-byte value only when the counter allows it.

name: call_four_routines_in_turn
description: Calls four routines in sequence and returns. It is a plain four-step sequence.

name: advance_pointer_on_zero
description: Decrements a countdown byte in a record and, when it reaches zero, advances a pointer in the record by twelve bytes; otherwise the pointer stays where it is. It steps through a sequence of fixed-size entries.

name: perform_four_sequential_calls
description: Calls four routines one after another and returns. It is a plain four-step sequence.

name: copy_record_and_write_dma
description: When a field in the source record is set, copies about fourteen bytes of the record to a destination, writes the argument to the DMA control register, clears the source field and sets a status byte in a linked block to minus one. It returns the argument rotated left by one bit.

name: run_four_routine_steps
description: Calls four routines in order and returns. It is a plain four-step sequence.

name: step_counter_on_timer_reload
description: Counts down a reload timer and, when it expires, steps a value in the record up or down within the range zero to sixty-three, depending on a mode byte. The new value is copied to a second record and the timer stops at the limit.

name: store_saved_or_default_value
description: When a flag byte is clear, stores a saved long value and count from the record if the count is non-zero, otherwise stores a default value with a count of one. It picks between two sources of a value.

name: invoke_four_routine_steps
description: Calls four routines in order and returns. It is a plain four-step sequence.

name: load_channel_block_set_dma
description: When a flag byte is set, writes the argument to the DMA control register, loads a block pointer from a table indexed by the record's channel number, copies fields from that block into the record and clears the flag. It switches the DMA channel to a new data block.

name: run_four_routine_steps
description: Calls four routines in order and returns. It is a plain four-step sequence.

name: dispatch_by_stored_index
description: Reads a byte index from the record, clears that byte and calls the routine selected from a jump table by that index. The referenced text looks like instruction bytes rather than a message.

name: set_shadow_flag_bit_one
description: Sets bit one of the shadow flag byte and returns. It marks one flag in the shadow control state.

name: store_position_offset_when_clear
description: When a status byte is clear, stores a value derived from the argument, with its low byte reduced by three, into a field of the current record and into a second record. It records an offset only when the status allows it.

name: map_block_to_channel_bit
description: Compares an address with four fixed block addresses spaced twenty bytes apart and writes the matching channel bit, one, two, four or eight, to the DMA control register. It maps a block to its DMA channel bit.

name: store_adjusted_byte_if_zero
description: When a byte field is zero, stores the argument byte minus eighty-six into it. It sets the field once and leaves it alone afterwards.

name: set_shadow_flag_bit_one
description: Sets bit one of the shadow flag byte and returns. It marks one flag in the shadow control state.

name: set_default_state_bytes
description: Clears one state byte and sets two further state bytes to the argument plus ninety. It initialises a small state record.

name: store_adjusted_byte_if_zero
description: When a byte field is zero, stores the argument byte minus eighty-six into it. It sets the field once and leaves it alone afterwards.

name: disable_low_dma_channels
description: Sets the shadow control byte to one and clears the lowest four DMA channel enable bits, which turns those DMA channels off.

name: describe_unresolved_routine
description: No pseudo-code could be produced for this routine, so its purpose is not known. The facts show a single instruction with no hardware register or text references.

name: return_immediately
description: A single return with no work.

description: A single return with no work.

name: return_immediately
description: A single return with no work.

name: set_copper_list_pointers
description: Writes the copper list location registers for the first and second copper lists. The decompiled body is unavailable, so only these register writes are known.

name: clear_and_xor_decode_stream
description: Initialises the interrupt and DMA control registers, clears a block of sixteen thousand long words and XOR-decodes a stream of records into it, using escape codes to repeat or skip bytes. It stops at its end marker and copies the decoded block to a second area after each pass.

name: run_frame_update_loop
description: Runs a loop that calls routines for each active object and advances per-object frame counters, branching on their values, and calls a pointer when a longword matches the text MON colon. The listing is cut off.

name: call_table_routine_keep_registers
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer held in a table at a fixed offset and returns the data registers unchanged. It forwards the call result.

name: call_routine_return_constant
description: Calls one routine and then returns the fixed value 131072. It ignores the routine's result.

name: patch_instructions_to_jsr
description: Scans memory up to an end address and replaces three specific instruction patterns with calls to three fixed low-memory addresses, patching the code in place. It redirects selected instructions to shared routines.

name: patch_custom_register_references
description: Scans a range of words and sets the top four bits of each word whose value falls inside the window around the custom chip register block. It adjusts stored references to the custom chip.

name: start_blit_and_wait
description: Writes a blitter size value to the blitter size register, then waits for the blitter to finish. It starts a blit and waits for it to complete.

name: halt_in_infinite_loop
description: Loops forever with no exit. The facts list a read of the video beam position, but the decompiled body is only the loop.

name: call_table_routine_keep_registers
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer held in a table at a fixed offset and returns the data registers unchanged. It forwards the call result.

name: init_display_and_decode_frame
description: Sets up interrupts and DMA, clears a block of memory, XOR-decodes a stream into it with the same escape codes as the other decoder and copies the result into a display area. The listing is cut off.

name: store_five_address_count_pairs
description: Stores five pairs of a 16-bit address and the count six into a fixed table, with the addresses stepping forward by forty. It initialises a table of five entries.

name: handle_timed_interrupt_event
description: Checks an interrupt request bit and, when it is set, sets a flag, advances a counter and, when the counter matches the next table entry, moves to the following entry and calls a routine.

name: wait_until_counter_exceeds
description: Waits for a counter field to change and then until it is greater than the argument, and clears the field. The inner loop compares the field with itself in the listing, so the exact exit condition is unclear.

name: update_audio_channels
description: Toggles a half-rate flag and, on alternate calls, reapplies saved DMA settings, then writes start address, length, period and volume for each of four audio channels from a table, counting down a delay field. It drives the four audio channels.

name: fill_pointer_table_then_run
description: Stores four pointers into a table spaced eighteen bytes apart from a fixed start, then calls four routines. It sets up the table and runs the steps that use it.

name: copy_channel_record_for_state
description: Computes a bit value from the signs of three state words, ORs it into a status word and, when the argument is below four, copies a stored record from a table into the output position. It selects a bit mask and copies the matching record.

name: negate_field_then_run_loop
description: Negates a 16-bit field and then enters the same frame update loop as its neighbouring routine. The listing is cut off.

name: install_interrupt_vectors_and_reset
description: Waits for a counter to reach 250, installs a routine at several interrupt vector addresses, clears interrupt and DMA enables by writing clear masks, resets the blitter masks and display control registers, then calls routines to finish setup.

name: store_long_and_set_flag
description: Stores a 32-bit argument into two consecutive words of memory and sets the shadow control byte to a fixed value. It saves a long value for later use.

name: record_beam_position_pair
description: Reads the video beam position twice and stores the first reading and the difference between the second reading and the first, minus one, into two consecutive words. It records a timing sample.

name: update_pseudo_random_state
description: Updates a 16-bit state with shifts, exclusive-or and an addition that uses a timer or beam position value, then returns the state with its halves swapped when one bit is clear. It produces a pseudo-random word and keeps the state for the next call.

name: read_joystick_directions_and_fire
description: Decodes the direction bits of the joystick port into four flags and reads the fire button from the shadow byte, detecting when it is pressed. It records the joystick state for the caller.

name: read_keyboard_serial_code
description: When a serial-ready flag is set, runs a handshake on the keyboard serial line, stores the incoming key code in a record field and waits for the line to clear. It reads one keyboard event.

name: copy_word_tables_to_shadow
description: Copies a sixteen-word table into the shadow buffer at two offsets and a fourteen-word table into a second buffer, then calls an optional routine and sets the shadow flag to a fixed value. It refreshes the shadow copies of its tables.

name: update_audio_playback_state
description: Checks a playback state and flag and, on the playback path, writes start address, length and volume for four audio channels from a table and updates the DMA control register. It refreshes audio output on each pass.

name: set_pointer_table_stepped
description: Writes four pointers starting from the argument, each spaced 36864 bytes apart, into a table, then stores a fixed value and a count of three in the next fields. It sets up a four-entry pointer table.

name: store_long_and_return
description: Stores a 32-bit argument into two words of memory and returns the same value. It records a value and passes it on.

name: set_row_pointer_table
description: Writes four addresses into a table, starting from a fixed address and spaced 1600 bytes apart. It sets the four addresses used by the caller.

name: clear_memory_block_longs
description: Clears a block of long words starting at a fixed address, running until a 16-bit counter wraps around, which covers a large block of memory.

name: step_scroll_offsets_toward_target
description: Compares a current and a target position in a control block, shifts three stored offsets by a step derived from a speed field, wraps them within a range and calls routines with the new offsets. When the values are equal it copies the current value and returns zero.

name: step_scroll_offsets_return_status
description: Compares a current and a target position in a control block and, when they differ, shifts three stored offsets by a step and wraps them within a range before calling routines. It returns a status value and copies the current position when finished.

name: copy_position_to_previous
description: Copies a stored position longword to the previous-position field of the same record.

name: blit_strips_for_position
description: Uses the blitter to copy tile strips for a position code below nine, then copies the current position to the previous-position field. It redraws the strips for one position.

name: blit_strips_for_inverse_position
description: Uses the blitter to copy tile strips for an inverted position code, then copies the current position to the previous-position field. It is the mirror case of its sibling routine.

name: step_scroll_offsets_by_speed
description: Adjusts three stored offsets by a step derived from a speed field, wraps them within a range, calls routines for the new offsets and copies the current position to the previous-position field. It advances the offsets by one speed step.

name: swap_buffer_offset_fields
description: Copies three offset longwords into working fields and then sets two output fields in an order chosen by a flag byte. It selects which offsets the next draw uses.

name: copy_offset_pair_to_output
description: Copies two working offset longwords into two output fields. It passes offsets on to the next stage.

name: blit_four_rows_with_offsets
description: Sets the blitter masks and modulo registers, then performs four blits at a fixed row spacing from two computed addresses. It copies a block of rows to the screen.

name: advance_scroll_offsets_wrapped
description: When a speed field is non-zero, adds a step to three stored offsets, wraps any offset above a limit back by a fixed amount, calls routines for the new offsets and copies the current position to the previous-position field. It advances the offsets by one speed step.

name: blit_two_rows_from_table
description: Uses the blitter to copy two rows of four blits each, with addresses derived from a position and a table value. It draws a small block of tiles.

name: copy_position_to_previous
description: Copies a stored position longword to the previous-position field of the same record.

name: dispatch_via_indexed_table
description: Calls a routine selected by a 16-bit index field in the record through a jump table. The jump table could not be recovered in the listing, so the target is not known.

name: toggle_offset_buffers
description: Copies three offset longwords into working fields, toggles a flag byte and copies two of the working values into output fields in an order set by the flag, calling a routine each time. It alternates between two offset buffers.

name: copy_output_offsets_and_call
description: Copies two working offset longwords into output fields and calls a routine. It passes offsets on to the next stage.

name: set_scroll_base_addresses
description: Sets three base addresses from fixed values offset by a value derived from the position, computes a mask from the low bits of the position and stores it, then copies the addresses to output fields according to a flag.

name: call_offset_table_entry
description: Calls a routine selected through a fixed table offset from a pointer taken from the caller. The jump table could not be recovered in the listing, so the target is not known.

name: fill_rows_then_dispatch
description: Fills a sequence of rows with values from a called routine, stepping by a stride between rows, then dispatches to a routine chosen from a jump table. The jump table could not be recovered in the listing.

name: combine_four_word_samples
description: Copies four words from a source at a fixed spacing into a destination and stores their bitwise OR in the first destination word. It combines four values into one word.

name: store_two_long_fields
description: Stores two long arguments into fixed fields of a record. It saves a pair of values.

name: store_first_word_and_dispatch
description: Stores a word into a record field and then calls a routine chosen from a jump table by the next word. The jump table could not be recovered in the listing.

name: store_second_word_and_dispatch
description: Stores a word into a second record field and then calls a routine chosen from a jump table by the next word. The jump table could not be recovered in the listing.

name: store_third_word_and_dispatch
description: Stores a word into a third record field and then calls a routine chosen from a jump table by the next word. The jump table could not be recovered in the listing.

name: decrement_colour_nibbles
description: Decrements each of the three four-bit fields of a 12-bit value by one, leaving a field that is already zero unchanged.

name: set_copper_list_and_jump
description: Stores two long arguments into record fields, sets the copper list pointer and calls a routine that restarts the copper, then copies the stored values to two output fields.

name: fill_sixteen_row_table
description: Repeats a pass of sixteen values for sixteen rows, filling a table with values from a called routine and advancing a row offset by 273 per pass. The listing is partly cut off, so not all branches are described.

name: return_immediately
description: A single return with no work.

name: step_nibbles_toward_target
description: Compares each four-bit field of the argument with the matching field of a stored word and adds one to any field that differs, returning the adjusted word. It moves a 12-bit value one unit per field toward a target.

name: init_copper_and_fill_table
description: Initialises timing and copper list fields, then runs a countdown loop that calls routines from a list until a flag is set, and fills a sixteen-by-two word table from calls to other routines. It sets the copper list pointer and restarts the copper.
